newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds near static waiting for Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds near static waiting for Wall Street.

text.p: Danish bond prices were near static on Wednesday in a market most interested in short-term two-five year paper with dealers foreseeing quiet conditions ahead waiting for the U.S. to open.
"There's nothing much expected to happen here until the American bond market opens," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down a marginal 0.02 point from the start at 106.16, yielding 7.07 percent in turnover of just under one billion crowns while its December future rose 0.32 point to 105.33 with 70 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.08 point to 83.48.
The crown traded at 3.8417 per mark at 1100 gmt, up from around 3.8427 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 93 basis points since the opening.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling small amounts of six percent 2002 bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
